label: pr-body-and-branch-state
name: PR body claims stale, contradicted or unusable; branch needs squash or rebase; ported file older than its source; earlier suggestion unapplied at the new push
description: What breaks: the reviewer reads a description of a different head. 5420005787 (PR 4557) is one review body with six findings that are the origin of checks 7-11 and 13: the required-CI-builds-AMX-off sentence contradicted by cmake-single-platform.yml:355 (check 7), unit-test and token-identity rows citing commits before the merge of main (check 8), assertion-count arithmetic, UTC timestamps and log paths (check 9), AMX tile constants and a t_heap_v2 alignment check that are not typed tensors (check 10), 20 commits with three rewording one Note (check 11, the only squash ask in 334 reviews), and value-suffixed constant names (check 13). 5371062950 adds the body being stale after several review rounds plus a merge conflict at approval; 4373886636 approves conditional on follow-ups and asks for a rebase; 3206111074 says a ported h/tron/gof.hpp is an old snapshot of hwattention_sync ('Be sure you are rebased to latest'); 3002050036 notes a typo suggestion from the earlier round still unapplied after a new push ('looks like this still needs fixed'). Procedure: run checks 7-11 and 13 at the final head; additionally compare the body's last edit against review-round commits; `gh pr view --json mergeable`; diff every file the body says is ported or copied against its source branch head; list unresolved suggestion threads whose original line still exists at HEAD; at approval state whether the body still describes the head.
disposition_reason: Checks 7-11 and 13 are subsumed as written; the stale-after-rounds, mergeability, ported-file freshness and unresolved-suggestion steps extend checks 8 and 11.
agent_feasibility: yes: all steps are gh and git queries plus the existing check procedures.

members.concern: The PR body carries passages a GitHub reader cannot use: assertion-count reconciliation arithmetic between revisions, UTC build timestamps and machine-local log paths; they should be removed.

detection.trigger: A Status/Verification/Tests/Results section of the PR body contains wall-clock times, machine-local paths or log names (/var/tmp/, /home/, *.log), or arithmetic reconciling counts between two revisions ('4 + 8192 = 8196', 'N fewer assertions than at X').
detection.procedure: save the body with gh pr view N --json body; grep -nE '[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}(:[0-9]{2})? ?(UTC|Z|PDT)|/var/tmp/|/home/|\.log|= *[0-9]+ *[+-]' inside those sections; for each hit ask whether deleting it changes any decision a reader who only has GitHub can make about the head.
detection.question: If the reviewer could only open GitHub, would deleting this clause change any decision about the head?

members.quote: Assertion-count arithmetic, UTC build timestamps and log paths can go.
members.note: Bullet 4c of 6 in review 5420005787. No author reply is in the digest; the live body text in the digest is truncated before the Status section, so whether the passages were removed cannot be read from the corpus. Wade approved the next head.

members.concern: At approval he notes that the PR body (description) no longer matches the code after several review rounds of changes, and that the branch has a merge conflict with main.

detection.trigger: The branch has review-driven commits after the PR body was last edited (compare the body's last edit time via gh api userContentEdits or the body text against commit subjects that say 'review round N'), or the body describes a mechanism the final head changed (e.g. body says counts are keyed by attention worker, head keys by pool worker); or `gh pr view N --json mergeable` returns CONFLICTING.
detection.procedure: Fetch `gh pr view N --json body,mergeable,mergeStateStatus`. List every mechanism sentence in the body (what is counted, keyed by what, who owns what, timer definitions, test counts, sample output). For each, grep the symbol or value at HEAD and check the sentence still holds; compare 'N cases' in the body with `grep -c TEST_CASE` in the test file at HEAD. Compare sample JSON in the body with the keys rendered at HEAD. Report the sentences that no longer hold. Separately report mergeable == CONFLICTING.
detection.question: Does every mechanism sentence and every count in the PR body hold at the final head, and does the branch merge cleanly into main?

members.quote: Approved... I think your PR description is stale at this point (after all the updates from reviews), and you currently have a merge conflict. But overall looks good.
members.note: Secondary pattern in the same text: merge-conflict-at-approval (`gh pr view --json mergeable`). The branch commit list ends with 'Merge branch main into jhan-attn-path-stats', so the conflict was resolved by a merge of main; the body was refreshed on 2026-09-30 (per memory pr4596-body-refresh-20260930). Existing check 9 covers unusable passages in Status/Verification sections only; check 8 covers stale result ids; neither covers mechanism prose that drifted after review rounds. He approved without re-reading the code at the new head.

members.concern: Approval conditioned on the author following up on the remaining minor inline comments, plus a note that the branch needs a rebase onto main.

detection.trigger: All inline comments are nits or answered questions, and the PR shows merge conflicts or is behind main (gh pr view --json mergeable,mergeStateStatus).
detection.procedure: Count open inline threads by severity; run gh pr view N --json mergeable,mergeStateStatus; if nothing blocks and the branch is behind or conflicting, the verdict is approve with 'follow up on the minor comments' and 'needs rebase'.
detection.question: Is every remaining thread a nit the author already agreed to, and is the branch mergeable as it stands?

members.quote: Overall looks good to me. Approved, assuming you'll follow up on the remaining minor comments. Also needs rebased.
members.note: Approved at commit cef0fb5b64, the commit his questions were on, before the author's fix commits; the head d4d6524dd5 contains the follow-ups ('Integrate review feedback and move from concurrencykit stall to mwait', 'Integrate review feedback.'). PR later closed unmerged; whether the rebase happened is not in the digest. He does not use the token LGTM.

members.concern: States that the copied header h/tron/gof.hpp is an outdated snapshot of the source branch hwattention_sync and asks the author to rebase onto its latest state, because Wade had since changed the gof/shard types when removing the singleton hw_attn_params.

detection.trigger: the PR body says the files are extracted, ported, cherry-picked or copied from another branch or PR ('from hwattention_sync', 'companion of', 'originally authored by'), or a new file's content exists on another branch
detection.procedure: identify the source branch from the body; `git diff <source-branch> -- <each new file>` (or `git log -1 <source-branch> -- <file>` to date the source); compare declarations named in the body ('per-shard hw_attn_params const*') against the source branch head; list symbols present on the source head but absent in the PR file
detection.question: does the PR's copy match the source branch at its current head, or an older revision of it?

members.quote: @BillBaumann this is an old version. Be sure you are rebased to latest `hwattention_sync`... gof/shard stuff changed up when I moved away from the 'singleton' hw_attn_params
members.note: The PR body claims 'The header reflects the post-redesign API: per-shard hw_attn_params const* hw_params rather than module-scope state', which Wade contradicts from his own knowledge of the source branch. Author replied 'rebaselining...'; Wade approved 16 hours later at a new commit b7ac03113f. An agent needs read access to the source branch (hwattention_sync) to reproduce it; the digest does not show which declarations differed (Insufficient data: diff of gof.hpp between 36cf204564 and hwattention_sync at 2026-05-08).

members.concern: Follow-up on his own typo suggestion (2983065535) three days later: the push since then did not apply it.

detection.trigger: A new push arrives after a review round; a suggestion block from the earlier round is still unresolved and the text at the new head still contains the original line.
detection.procedure: For each earlier inline suggestion thread, fetch the suggested line and grep the file at the new head for the original (pre-suggestion) text; if still present, re-raise in the same thread.
detection.question: Does the file at the new head still contain the line the suggestion replaced?

codex_bullets.bullet: Trace each changed area to the stated behavior or an explicitly requested bundled change. Suggest splitting unrelated cleanup. A missing body sentence alone does not make a necessary regression test unrelated.
codex_bullets.reason: Five comments (PRs 4557, 1920, 2148, 2659, 3016). Claude check 10 has the full procedure; the third sentence matches check 10's "regression guard" clause.

codex_bullets.bullet: Name the actual CI workflow, trigger, effective configuration, and runner when claiming coverage. A packaging or manually invoked workflow may not gate the PR.
codex_bullets.reason: One Wade comment (PR 4557) plus the 3879 paste. Claude check 7 lists lanes, triggers and configure lines.

codex_bullets.bullet: Label results with their tested revision and relevant configuration. Keep usable artifact references and outcomes. Remove obsolete arithmetic and local bookkeeping that do not help a reviewer assess the change.
codex_bullets.reason: Three comments (PRs 4557, 4596, 2713; 5420005787 quoted twice). Claude checks 8 and 9 cover revision labels and unusable passages.

codex_bullets.bullet: Follow current repository and user conventions. Wade's naming and formatting preferences are usually nits. His later acceptance of value suffixes in established kernel code does not prescribe them for shared code.
codex_bullets.reason: Five comments (PRs 4557, 2089, 2287, 2011); naming nits are frequent (also 2982403509, 2941290531). The corpus shows Wade did raise the suffix for shared code; the Claude skill should narrow "never a finding" to the author's kernel files.
codex_bullets.claude_skill_coverage: partial (check 13 covers stems; it declares the value suffix "never a finding", which 6021333114 contradicts for shared code)

codex_bullets.bullet: Treat commit cleanup as reviewability and history hygiene. Repeated fixups or unrelated commits can justify a suggestion. Commit count alone does not. Do not invent an owner-approval gate from file authorship; report an explicit unresolved request or repository requirement when one exists.
codex_bullets.reason: Three comments (PRs 4557, 2766). The one owner request in the corpus (4188336279) is tied to the commit origin, not to file blame; see contradictions.
codex_bullets.claude_skill_coverage: covered (checks 11, 12); check 12 derives the owner set from file authorship, which the codex bullet forbids

codex_bullets.bullet: Do not turn an approved follow-up into a blocker.
codex_bullets.reason: Five comments (PRs 2766, 3490, 4267, 2980, 2176). Wade approves with follow-ups often (100 of 334 reviews approved, 0 changes requested); one sentence in the Claude skill would stop an agent from escalating these.
codex_bullets.claude_skill_coverage: partial (severity words listed; no rule about follow-ups)

codex_bullets.bullet: Read the PR metadata with `gh pr view N ... --json title,body,headRefOid,baseRefName,baseRefOid,commits,reviews`. Resolve the comparison from the actual target branch and reviewed commit, including stacked PRs. Do not hardcode `origin/main`.
codex_bullets.reason: One comment (PR 2676) shows a PR whose target was the hwattention_sync branch, not main; many 2026 PRs in the corpus targeted that branch. The Claude BASE definition is wrong for them; see contradictions.
codex_bullets.claude_skill_coverage: partial (setup 1 fixes HEAD and BASE but defines BASE as merge-base with origin/main)

codex_bullets.bullet: For CI, follow the workflow trigger and any reusable-workflow caller; trace effective build options through presets, recipes and defaults; use `gh pr checks N --required`; do not equate a workflow's existence with a required check, or compilation with execution.
codex_bullets.reason: One Wade comment (PR 4557) plus the 3879 paste. Claude check 7 has the fuller procedure.

codex_bullets.bullet: For a result, resolve its commit and compare changed paths against HEAD. Label an older run. If a commit cannot be resolved, report missing provenance; do not invent a rebase or amendment history.
codex_bullets.reason: One comment (PR 4557). Claude check 8 covers it, including unresolvable ids.

codex_bullets.bullet: Use the diff and dependencies to decide whether a hunk belongs. Commit subjects, authors, matching identifiers, and text similarity are search aids, not proof. Necessary tests and adaptations remain in scope even if the description needs improvement.
codex_bullets.reason: One comment (PR 4557). Claude check 10 already requires BASE-content evidence before clearing or reporting; the subject-verb binning is a priority order, not proof. See contradictions for the wording.
codex_bullets.claude_skill_coverage: covered (check 10); check 10 bins commits by subject verb and author, which this bullet calls search aids only

codex_bullets.bullet: Use commit history to identify repeated fixups. Current blame cannot show superseded edits. Consider the intended merge method and the author's stated cleanup plan. Do not require squashing solely because there are many commits.
codex_bullets.reason: Two comments (PRs 4557, 2766); the corpus has exactly one squash request. Claude check 11 already says "Commit count alone" is not a finding.
